newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai bank to launch phone transaction service.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai bank to launch phone transaction service.

text.p: Shanghai's Bank of Communications is planning to set up a 24-hour telephone banking service for foreign currency transactions to help boost business, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.
The newspaper said the 24-hour service would make it possible for clients to trade on overseas markets.
It quoted bank president Xu Jiasheng as saying the bank would also provide more loan support for booming industry sectors such as biotechnology and pharmaceuticals during 1997.
The bank will also look at providing more syndicated loans to multi-nationals operating in Shanghai in association with foreign banks, the newspaper said.
The Bank of Communications, China's only major state bank based in Shanghai, posted a 25 percent rise in local currency loans in 1996 over the previous year, it said.
It said the bank's assets last year were valued at 47.4 billion yuan, 11.8 percent more than in 1995.
